doc_verification.detail: Reachability: no doc_preflight.json sidecar exists in the contract tree; sanctioned WebFetch failed with an environment network restriction for api.qdrant.tech, but the page was recovered via the alternate web reader with full content — page IS reachable, so PASS recorded honestly with the WebFetch block noted. Version: page served under v-1-18-x selector = 1.18.x vs target 1.18.0, major.minor match. Content: doc Query parameters section verbatim 'timeout integer Optional `>=1` Defaults to `60`' / 'Timeout for this request' — exact match with the contract assertion 'timeout default 60, minimum 1'; page documents only '200 Retrieved' (no 500 documented, no standalone-mode caveat prose). Endpoint: contract endpoint_registry entry cluster+telemetry GET lists timeout (integer, 'default 60, min 1') and details_level (integer), and raw_knowledge api_endpoints maps cluster+telemetry -> /cluster/telemetry, matching the tested REST face.

execution_evidence.log_pattern: [class-B timeout='+1'] status=500 raw={"status":{"error":"Service internal error: Could not get telemetry from cluster"},"time":0.000209122} (output_boundary_cluster_telemetry_002.log L20, followed by [healthz attempt 1] status=200 raw=healthz check passed L21)
secondary_observations: class-A conforming rejections (same log L6-L19, rest face): timeout='abc'/'1.5'/'true'/'1e3'/' 1'/'0x10' each -> status=400 {"status":{"error":"Deserialize error in query parameters: invalid digit found in string"},"time":0.0}; timeout='' -> 400 'cannot parse integer from empty string' — every type-invalid token properly rejected 4xx

hidden Type2 leg suppressed by rank ordering (script findings rank1-Type3 beat rank2-Type2; verifiable from raw bodies): the class-A 400 bodies do NOT name the violated parameter ('timeout' absent from 'Deserialize error in query parameters: invalid digit found in string')

baseline confound, sibling output_boundary_cluster_telemetry_001.log L7 (rest face): [timeout omitted (default-60 form)] params=None status=500 raw={"status":{"error":"Service internal error: Could not get telemetry from cluster"},"time":0.003408097} — the documented-valid baseline ALSO 500s

same-value control, sibling output_boundary_cluster_telemetry_001.log L9 (rest face): [timeout=1 (min closure)] params={'timeout': 1} status=500 raw={"status":{"error":"Service internal error: Could not get telemetry from cluster"},"time":0.000267159} — the plain in-domain integer 1 (what '+1' deserializes to) gets the identical 500, so '+1' is not the operative cause

sign-grammar asymmetry, sibling output_boundary_cluster_telemetry_001.log L17 (rest face): [timeout=-1] params={'timeout': -1} status=400 raw={"status":{"error":"Deserialize error in query parameters: invalid digit found in string"},"time":0.0} — u64 rejects '-' but accepts '+' prefix, corroborating that '+1' parsed to integer 1 and reached the handler

minimum validation present, sibling output_boundary_cluster_telemetry_001.log L15 (rest face): [timeout=0 (min-1)] params={'timeout': 0} status=422 raw={"status":{"error":"Validation error in query parameters: [timeout: value 0 invalid, must be 1 or larger]"},"time":0.0} — the 422 body DOES name 'timeout'

second baseline, sibling output_boundary_cluster_telemetry_004.log L7 (rest face): [documented no-param call] params=None status=500 raw={"status":{"error":"Service internal error: Could not get telemetry from cluster"},"time":0.000164451}

deployment-mode proof, sibling output_boundary_cluster_recover_001.log L15 (rest face): [recover] status=500 raw={"status":{"error":"Service internal error: Qdrant is running in standalone mode"},"time":0.024100829} — the sandbox runs a standalone single-node qdrant

http_semantics.note: Request-side-decidable errors were NOT masked as 2xx: all seven type-invalid timeout tokens returned proper 400 with serde diagnostics, and timeout=0 returned 422 naming the parameter and rule. The observed 500 is an internal error returned for a fully valid request ('+1' deserializes to in-domain 1), not a business-code-masked client error.

triggering_scripts: boundary_cluster_telemetry_004 (documented no-param call and details_level=0 -> identical 500)

contract_grounding.note: violates-declaration self-check: the claim's phenomenon is a 5xx on an in-domain value, not an illegal value silently accepted. '+1' deserializes to integer 1, which satisfies 'minimum 1'; source implements both faces of the assertion (range(min=1) validator at cluster_api.rs:45 — behaviorally confirmed by the 422 on timeout=0 — and default 60 at cluster_api.rs:236 via DEFAULT_GRPC_TIMEOUT=60s). The value is genuinely compliant, so the range constraint was not violated by this behavior. The expectation actually failed by the 500 is the sibling behavioral assertion qdrant_behavioral_cluster_telemetry_001 ('returns 200 TelemetryData') — which fails for ALL inputs in this deployment including the documented no-param baseline (sibling log 004) — noted for the auditor; the wrong-constraint alternative would be re-anchoring to that behavioral assertion, which is the auditor's call.

chain_links: contract: qdrant_range_cluster_telemetry_001 exists in structured_contract.json (L6458-6468; range_constraint; endpoint cluster+telemetry; assertion 'timeout default 60, minimum 1'; source_url versioned api-reference; source_status reachable). Dispatch constraint_id was truncated to 'qdra'; resolved to the full id via the script docstring (debate_logs/boundary_cluster_telemetry_002.py L34 'Constraint: qdrant_range_cluster_telemetry_001').

doc: https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/distributed/cluster-telemetry reachable (recovered via alternate web reader after the sanctioned WebFetch hit an environment network block) and contains verbatim 'timeout integer Optional `>=1` Defaults to `60`' — prose matches the assertion; only 200 Retrieved documented, no 500 and no standalone caveat.

script: debate_logs/boundary_cluster_telemetry_002.py — GET {BASE_URL}/cluster/telemetry with requests params={'timeout': '+1'} (URL-encoded %2B1); log L5 constraint quote matches the contract assertion verbatim; oracle pre-declared class-B '+1' 5xx-with-live-healthz = Type3 DEFECT, 4xx/200 both conform.

log: output_boundary_cluster_telemetry_002.log L20-L22 — raw 500 body quoted matches the verdict DEFECT_FOUND (Type3_RuntimeFailure) exactly; internally consistent. Attribution caveat (not a link break): the identical 500 occurs for documented-valid baselines in sibling logs 001/004, so the 500 is the endpoint's uniform response in this deployment rather than a '+1'-specific runtime fault — see secondary_observations and mundane_explanation.

grep_queries: Could not get telemetry from cluster
source_grounding.call_chain_traced: GET /cluster/telemetry -> actix Query<ClusterTelemetryParams> (serde_urlencoded u64 deserialization; '+1' accepted as 1 per Rust integer FromStr sign grammar, '-' rejected — behaviorally corroborated by 400 on '-1' in sibling log 001 L17) -> validator range(min=1) passes for 1 (422 only for 0, sibling log 001 L15) -> get_cluster_telemetry (cluster_api.rs L203) reads channel_service.id_to_address, which init_channel_service (main.rs L299-315) leaves EMPTY in single-node mode -> zero peer futures -> empty telemetries -> resolve_telemetries (distributed_telemetry.rs L150-158) -> newest_telemetry(&[]) = None -> StorageError::service_error("Could not get telemetry from cluster") -> HTTP 500 for every request reaching the handler, independent of the timeout value.
source_grounding.by_design_note: The standalone-empty-peer 500 has NO explicit design declaration: no comment, docstring, or maintainer citation in the handler or resolve_telemetries marks standalone behavior as intended (contrast: cluster_api.rs L23-25 carries an explicit TODO for details_level, and sibling endpoints L125/L146 return the distinct 'Qdrant is running in standalone mode' error via consensus_state()-None guards — the telemetry handler lacks any such guard). Not marked by_design_in_source; outcome recorded as validation_present for the cited range constraint, with the 500 mechanism explained but its defect-vs-environment status left to the auditor.

excluded: concurrency (deterministic sub-millisecond responses, /healthz 200 on first attempt across all 5 telemetry logs, no shared state involved)
request-parameter typo (script echoes exact params; requests encoded '+1' as %2B1)
cache delay (no caching semantics on this read-only ops endpoint; failure immediate and stable)
mundane_explanation.surviving: environment/deployment mode: the sandbox qdrant runs standalone (proven by sibling recover log's 'Qdrant is running in standalone mode' 500), and in single-node mode init_channel_service leaves the peer map empty, making GET /cluster/telemetry return 500 'Could not get telemetry from cluster' for EVERY request including the documented no-param baseline — the '+1' token is not the operative cause of the 500. Cannot be fully excluded at raw-access level because a distributed deployment was not available to test the 200 path (face_unavailable: single deployment mode in sandbox); counterpoint for the auditor: the same contract marks cluster+status as 'valid on single-node deployments too' and that endpoint DOES return 200 here, while the cluster-telemetry doc documents only 200 with no standalone caveat and no 500 — whether an unconditionally-500ing documented-200 endpoint on standalone is a genuine defect or an environment artifact is the auditor's adjudication.
